info.title: Mila API
info.description:
Mila's REST API. The Go server and the TypeScript client are both
generated from this file (make generate), so it is the contract.

Signing in sets an HttpOnly session cookie. Requests that change data
with that cookie must come from Mila's own origin.

Sync also has a WebSocket at /api/v1/sync/ws, outside this file. It
carries only nudges: {"type":"poke","workspace":id,"seq":n} when a
workspace has changes to pull, {"type":"workspaces"} when the user's
memberships changed, {"type":"notify"} when their notifications
changed (a new one, or one read on another device), {"type":"settings"}
when their preferences changed, {"type":"themes","id":id} when one of
their own themes was saved or deleted (the app loads that one again),
{"type":"people"} when someone they
share a workspace with changed their name or picture, and
{"type":"reset","workspace":id}
when what they may see in a workspace changed (a guest given or denied
a project): the app pulls, the pull answers 410, and the app loads the
workspace afresh.

Calendar feeds are served at /ical/<token>.ics, also outside this file
and without a session: the token in the link is the key. A feed is
text/calendar (RFC 5545) with a strong ETag, and answers 404 once it
is revoked or its owner can no longer see what it shows.

A script or another app authenticates with a personal API token, made
in Settings, API tokens, and sent as Authorization: Bearer <token>. It
acts as its owner, read only or read and write, in one workspace or
all of theirs. It reaches the rows below with a task's activity and
attachments and a page's versions and attachments; and, to read only,
GET /me, GET /workspaces, a workspace and its people, members and
trash; and exports, with a token that can write. Anything else (the
rest of /me among it) answers 403 token_not_allowed, and a token that
is not valid answers 401 invalid_token. Webhooks, in Settings, Webhooks, are
the other way: Mila tells an address when something changes.

Every synced entity (projects, statuses, labels, custom fields, saved
views, tasks and what hangs off them) can also be read and written a
row at a time under /workspaces/{workspaceId}/<collection>. These are
generated from the server's entity registry. Rows are flat JSON with
the same snake_case fields sync uses, plus read-only id, created_at
and updated_at. A write is one sync operation through the same merge
as the app's: the same checks and permissions, the same history and
notifications, and every open device sees it at once. Each field is
last writer wins, stamped by the server's clock (or just after the
newest write it replaces); send If-Match with a row's ETag to change
it only if it is unchanged since you read it. An Idempotency-Key on a
POST or PATCH makes a retry safe: it is kept 90 days, and a retry
answers with the row as it stands then rather than a replay; a key
sent again with another body is not noticed. A Mila-Batch header (1 to
64 letters, digits and dashes, of your choosing) on a POST, PATCH or
DELETE groups the write with others under that name: automations count
the batch once toward a rule's hourly limit, and POST
/workspaces/{workspaceId}/actions/undo-batch puts the whole batch back
for 30 days. Lists come a page at a
time in ID order. A script that uses the session cookie must send
Origin with this server's origin on every request that changes data.
Reads are limited to 1,200 a minute and writes to 300 a minute for
each person, after a burst of twice as many.

These endpoints change one row each. What the app does as one action
takes several, which you make yourself:

- A new project has no statuses; the app makes Backlog, To do, In
  progress, Done and Canceled.
- Completing a task in a project sets completed_at and moves it to
  a done status, and reopening it moves it back to a to-do status;
  moving it to a done or canceled status sets completed_at too.
- Completing a repeating task also sets its series_id (its own ID,
  when it has none) and makes the next task of the series; through
  the API nothing makes the next one.
- To move a task to another project, PATCH its project_id and
  status_id together (a status of the new project, or null), then do
  the same for each of its subtasks: a subtask must stay in its
  parent's project, and until it follows, changes to it are refused.
- Deleting a status leaves its tasks pointing at it; the app moves
  them to another status of the project first.
- A reminder made relative to the due moment (offset_minutes) fires
  at the due moment less the offset whatever its remind_at says, so
  changing a due date needs no change to it; the app updates
  remind_at only to show it.

tags.name: actions
tags.description: What the app does as one action, done on the server in one request: the ops it would make, each through the same merge and checks as a row's write. Made for scripts and agents (docs/agents.md). Wherever an action takes a project, status, label or person it takes a name too, matched without regard to case among what you can see; a name that matches nothing or more than one thing is refused, with the candidates. Send Mila-Batch to group an action's ops with other writes; without one, an action names its own batch in its answer, which undo-batch undoes.

tags.name: projects
tags.description: A project: a list of tasks with its own statuses. A new project has no statuses; make them too (the app makes Backlog, To do, In progress, Done and Canceled).

tags.name: statuses
tags.description: A step a project's tasks move through, in a category that says what it means (done and canceled close a task).

tags.name: labels
tags.description: A label any task in the workspace can carry. Every member sees every label, guests too.

tags.name: custom-fields
tags.description: A field of the user's own on tasks: in one project, or with no project_id, in every project.

tags.name: saved-views
tags.description: A saved filter and how it lays out what it shows. With owner_id set, only its owner sees it.

tags.name: tasks
tags.description:
A task: in a project or, with no project_id, in the inbox; with parent_id, a subtask, which lives in its parent's project.

To move a task with subtasks to another project, move the parent first (project_id, with a status_id of the new project, or null), then each subtask the same way. Until a subtask is moved it stays where it was and can still be edited there; a write that sets a subtask's project_id or parent_id is refused unless it puts the subtask in its parent's project.

tags.name: task-labels
tags.description: A label on a task. Its ID is made from the pair, so adding the same label again brings back the same row.

tags.name: task-dependencies
tags.description: A task waiting for another to be done (blocked by it): task_id waits for blocker_id. The two may be in different projects of the workspace; a guest sees the row only when they see both tasks. Its ID is made from the pair, as a label's on a task is. A dependency that would close a loop (the blocker already waits for the task, directly or down a chain) is refused.

tags.name: task-assignees
tags.description: A member assigned to a task. Its ID is made from the pair, as a label's on a task is.

tags.name: checklist-items
tags.description: A step of a task's checklist.

tags.name: comments
tags.description: A comment on a task. Only its author changes it; admins may delete it.

tags.name: pages
tags.description:
A wiki page: in a project's wiki, or with no project_id, the workspace's (which guests do not see). A wiki's main page has no parent_id and an ID made from its project's or workspace's ID (XOR with 2f5c6c0e-8a9b-4c7e-9d3a-6b1e4f2a7c58); it cannot be deleted, and its title is not shown, since it takes its project's or workspace's name. Every other page has a parent_id in the same wiki. Deleting a page does not delete its subpages: delete them too.

body is Markdown, written as the editor writes it (checklists, tables, images, and boxes as > [!NOTE]); a write replaces it whole and is kept as a version of its own in the page's history (GET .../pages/{pageId}/versions). A link to a page is a link to its address in the app (/wiki?page=<id>, or /projects/<projectId>?tab=wiki&page=<id>) and to a task is /?task=<id>; when either is renamed, links whose text was its old name take the new one. An image of a file attached to the page or a task is ![name](/api/v1/workspaces/<workspaceId>/attachments/<attachmentId>/file).

tags.name: page-threads
tags.description: Comments pinned to some words of a wiki page. Anyone who can read the page can comment and can resolve or reopen a thread. Only an owner or admin can delete one that holds other people's comments.

tags.name: page-comments
tags.description: A comment in a thread on a wiki page. Only its author changes it; admins may delete it.

tags.name: attachments
tags.description: A file on a task. Upload one with POST /workspaces/{workspaceId}/tasks/{taskId}/attachments, and fetch its bytes from .../attachments/{attachmentId}/file.

tags.name: page-attachments
tags.description: A file on a wiki page, as an attachment is on a task. Upload one with POST /workspaces/{workspaceId}/pages/{pageId}/attachments, and fetch its bytes from /workspaces/{workspaceId}/attachments/{attachmentId}/file, as a task's.

tags.name: page-drawings
tags.description: A drawing in a wiki page, which the page's body names with <!-- mila:drawing <id> --> and a picture of it. Its shapes are drawing_shape rows. A page holds 50 drawings at most.

tags.name: drawing-shapes
tags.description: A shape of a drawing: a box, ellipse, diamond, cylinder, text, sticky note, line, arrow, pen stroke or picture, with its place, words and look. A line or arrow on shapes names them in from_id and to_id and follows them. Shapes are drawn in sort_key order. A drawing holds 2,000 shapes at most.

tags.name: my-day-entries
tags.description: A task in the user's My Day, which only they see. Its ID is made from the task and the user.

tags.name: reminders
tags.description: A reminder on a task, which only its owner sees and gets.

tags.name: custom-field-values
tags.description: A task's value for a custom field. Its ID is made from the task and the field.

tags.name: templates
tags.description: A project, a task or a wiki page saved to make more from, as the app's Settings, Templates shows them. Members and admins see a workspace's templates; guests never do. data is the snapshot; the app makes the rows from it.

tags.name: time-entries
tags.description: Time logged on a task by one person: typed in, or a timer. A timer runs while running is true, its minutes 0 until it stops; set running to false with minutes, the time since started_at, to stop it. A person has one timer running at a time, so the app stops any other first. Its person changes it, and so do admins. Everyone who sees the task sees its time.

tags.name: project-time-entries
tags.description: Time logged to a project itself by one person, not to one of its tasks: a meeting, planning, travel. Typed in, or a timer, as a time entry is on a task: a timer runs while running is true, its minutes 0 until it stops. A person has one timer running at a time, on a task or a project, so the app stops any other first. Its person changes it, and so do admins. Everyone who sees the project sees its time.

tags.name: workspace-themes
tags.description: A theme the workspace offers everyone in it, guests too, as the app's Settings, Workspace themes shows them: nobody is switched to one. Owners and admins publish, change and unpublish them (set deleted_at); a workspace offers 10 at most.

tags.name: automations
tags.description: A rule: when something happens to a task, and it fits, the changes someone chose. Not for guests.

get.description: This file, as JSON. The reference at /api/docs reads it.
Whether the instance still needs setting up, and who is signed in.

post.description: Creates the first user from the one-time link the server printed, and signs them in.
Emails a sign-in link if the address has an account. Succeeds either way.

The address a sign-in link signs in to, without spending it, so the
link's page can ask before switching a browser signed in to
another account.
Signs in with the token from a sign-in link. Each token works once.

get.description: Signs in the desktop app's window on this computer, with the key the app started the server with, which works once. Only in that mode. Redirects to the app.

What the desktop app needs of a place on this computer whose window is showing another place: how many workspaces it has, and the notifications made since the last time it asked, still unread, so the app can show them on the desktop. With the watch key the app started the server with, in X-Mila-Watch, which lasts as long as the server. Only in that mode. With no after, it says only where to start.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: The cursor the last answer gave.

post.description: Makes the one-time code a signed-in browser hands to the desktop app on the same computer. It needs a recent sign-in. Not open to a token.

challenge.description: The base64url SHA-256 of a secret only the app holds.

post.description: Signs in the desktop app's window with a code and the secret behind it. Each code is good for one try, within a few minutes.

Makes the address a change-of-address link was sent to the
account's own, with the token from that link. It needs no session:
the link proves the address. Each token works once, for 24 hours,
and only the newest one a person asked for works. Sign-in links for
the old address stop working, and the old address is told.

200.description: The account, with its new address.

patch.description: Changes your name. Up to 30 changes an hour, after a burst of 10.

put.description:
Sets your picture. Send a PNG of 16 to 1024 pixels on a side and
4 MB at most. Mila crops the middle square, scales it to 256
pixels at most and encodes it again (JPEG when it is opaque, PNG
when it has transparency), which drops any metadata. Up to 30
changes an hour (removals included), after a burst of 10.

delete.description: Removes your picture; your initials show instead. It counts toward the 30 picture changes an hour.

get.description:
A person's picture, as the avatar field of a User, Member,
AdminUser, ProjectGuest or Notification names it. Only they, the
people they share a workspace with and instance admins may see it;
anyone else gets 404, as for a key that names nothing. A new
picture has a new key, so a response may be cached for a year.

304.description: Unchanged since the ETag sent in If-None-Match.

post.description:
Emails a link to a new address for the caller's account. The
address changes only when the link is opened (see
confirmEmailChange). Refused (409) for an address another account
uses, and past 5 links in an hour. Needs a sign-in from the last 10
minutes: an older session gets 403 with the code sign_in_again.

Deletes the caller's account, for good. The personal workspace goes,
and so does every shared workspace where the caller is the only
member; in shared workspaces with others, what the caller wrote
stays, credited to "Deleted user", and their assignments end. It is
refused (409) while the caller is the only owner of a shared
workspace others use, or the instance's only admin. Every session
ends; the response clears the cookie. Needs a sign-in from the last
10 minutes: an older session gets 403 with the code sign_in_again.

get.description: The caller's exports, newest first. Finished ones can be downloaded for 7 days.
A finished export's zip, for the caller who made it.
The caller's imports, newest first.

post.description:
Uploads a JSON export's zip and imports it into a new workspace owned
by the caller, in the background; the workspace appears when it is
complete. ids keep restores every row under its own ID, refused
if any is already on this instance; fresh gives every row a new one.

put.description: Records the time zone of the user's device, for reminders, due notices, the digest and the weekly report, and how it writes dates and times.

clock.description: How the device writes times, which is what an "auto" clock preference means in emails and notifications.

dateOrder.description: How the device writes dates, for an "auto" date format preference.

weekStart.description: The device's first day of the week, 0 for Sunday to 6 for Saturday, for an "auto" week start in the weekly report. Left out, the one reported before stays.

patch.description:
Changes the preferences the body names and leaves the others as
they are, so devices that each changed a different one keep both.
The user's other devices are told to reload them. Nothing is
saved if any value is not allowed.

get.description: Your own themes, oldest first.
One of your themes. Another person's answers 404, as one that does not exist.

put.description:
Makes or replaces one of your themes; the id in the body must be
the one in the address. The whole theme is replaced, so the later
of two saves wins, and saving a deleted theme makes it again. A
theme that is not exactly right (an unknown token, a value out of
bounds, a number sent as text) answers 400 and saves nothing. You
may keep 20 themes of up to 16 KiB each; a new one past that
answers 400 with the error too_many_themes. Your other devices are
told (the themes message).

delete.description:
Deletes one of your themes. If your preferences name it
(customTheme), the app shows the built-in theme it was based on.

get.description: The caller's notifications, newest first, a page at a time, with how many are unread.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: The next cursor from the previous page.

post.description: Marks the caller's notifications read, up to and including the newest one they have seen, so one that arrived meanwhile stays unread.

through.description: The ID of the newest notification the caller has loaded.

get.description: What the workspace's automations did lately, newest first, for one automation or all of them. Kept for 30 days. Not for guests.

post.description: Deletes the caller's notifications, up to and including the newest one they have seen, so one that arrived meanwhile stays.

through.description: The ID of the newest notification they have seen.

delete.description: Deletes one of the caller's notifications, for good. Asking again, or for one that isn't theirs, changes nothing.

put.description:
Replaces the caller's preferences. Mentions and reminders always
show in the app, whatever is sent.

post.description: Emails the caller a test message, three at once and then three an hour at most.

get.description: The key browsers subscribe with, and how many of the caller's devices get pushes.

post.description:
Turns on push for the caller's browser, for as long as this session
lasts: signing out stops it. A browser that subscribes again (with
new keys, or as someone else) replaces its earlier subscription.
Turns off push for one of the caller's browsers.
Pushes a test message to each of the caller's devices at once, five at once and then one a minute at most.

200.description: What happened on the caller's devices.
Signed-in devices, most recently used first.

get.description: The caller's security log, newest first: sign-ins, new devices, accepted invitations, passkeys added and removed, devices signed out and admin rights given or taken. Kept for a year.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: The ID of the last event of the page before; omitted for the newest.

post.description:
Starts adding a passkey. Adding one needs a sign-in from the last 10
minutes, here and when finishing: an older session gets 403 with
the code sign_in_again.

delete.description:
Removes one of the caller's passkeys and emails them that it is gone.
Needs a sign-in from the last 10 minutes, with a passkey while the
account has one: an older session, or one from an email link, gets
403 with the code sign_in_again.

get.description: Who the asker can see in the workspace, by name and picture, with no email addresses, for naming people and for mentions. Members see everyone. A guest sees the members and the guests who share a project with them. A guest's projects are those they are given, as far as the asker may know, so a list of who can reach a task can be worked out from this.
People whose work (comments, files, tasks) is in the workspace but who no longer belong to it, so it keeps a name: those who left, and deleted accounts, named "Deleted user".
How many members use each theme the workspace offers (its workspace_theme rows), by theme id; it names no one. Owners and admins only.

post.description: Starts an export of what the caller sees of the workspace, in the background. When it is ready the caller gets a notification, and it can be downloaded for 7 days. One person may have three on the way and ten kept at once (deleting one makes room), and start ten an hour; none starts while the server is low on disk space.

get.description: The workspace's guests and whether each is given the project. Members see every project already. Admins and owners only.

put.description: Gives a guest the project. Their devices load the workspace afresh and the project's tasks arrive.

delete.description: Takes the project from a guest. Their devices load the workspace afresh, and the project's tasks disappear from them.
Removes a member, or leaves the workspace when the user is the caller.

get.description:
Every live row of the workspace the caller may see, and the change
number they reflect. An app that syncs another schema version, or
names none, is answered 426 with the code update_required, so that
it reloads before it reads what it may not know how to keep.

Changes after a change number, a page at a time. 410 Gone means the
device is out of step and must bootstrap again: the server was
restored from a backup (the epoch differs), or the device has not
pulled for longer than the change log keeps changes (30 days).

parameters.name: epoch
parameters.description: The epoch from the device's last bootstrap; missing or different answers 410.

post.description:
Applies operations in order and reports on each. A push from an app
that syncs another schema version is refused whole, before any
operation is applied, with 426 and the code update_required; the
app keeps its operations and sends them once it has reloaded. One
that names a user other than the session's is refused whole with
409 and the code other_user: the browser has signed in as someone
else since the edits were made.

schema.description: The app's version of the synced entities (SYNC_SCHEMA).

user.description: The ID of the person the operations were made as, when the sender knows it; left out, the session's.

200.description: One result per operation, in order.

get.description: Projects, tasks, wiki pages and templates deleted in the last 30 days, newest first. Restore one by syncing deleted_at back to null.

post.description: Adds a task as the app does: in a project, in its to-do status unless one is named; a subtask in its parent's project; then its labels, assignees and checklist. Everything named is found before anything is written, so a name that matches nothing makes nothing.
Completes a task as checking it off does: in a project its status moves to done, and a repeating task's next one is made (answered as next).
Reopens a completed task: in a project it goes back to a to-do status. A repeating task's next one, if made, stays.
Moves a task to a status of its project, by ID or name, or to the project's first status of a kind. A done or canceled status completes it (making a repeating task's next one); any other reopens it.
Moves a task, with its subtasks, to another project or to the Inbox (project null), each to the status of the same kind there. A subtask moves only with its task.

Gives a task to people, by ID or name (me for you), or with remove takes it off them. Everyone named is found, and able to reach the task (a guest only in the projects shared with them), before anything is written.
Puts labels of the workspace on a task, by ID or name, or with remove takes them off.
Makes a project with the app's five starting statuses (Backlog, To do, In progress, Done, Canceled), or with the statuses given, in their order.
Deletes a status after moving its tasks to another status of the project: the one named in to, else the first of the same kind, else the first.
Adds text at the end of a task's notes or a page's body. It is written from the text as it stands on the server, and tried again if someone typed meanwhile, so nothing they wrote is lost.

Replaces what is under a heading in a task's notes or a page's body, down to the next heading of the same or a higher level, or adds the section at the end if there is no such heading. The rest, Mila's markers included, is left as it is. Written as append-notes is.

get.description: Reads a task with its status, project, labels and assignees named, its checklist in order, its comments oldest first with their authors named, and its subtasks. A task in the trash is read too, with in_trash true. A read-only token may use it.

parameters.name: task
parameters.description: The task's ID.

get.description: Lists the tasks you can see that match every part given, soonest due first, each with its status, project, labels and assignees named. Dates are in your time zone, and today is given in the answer. Tasks in archived projects stay out unless that project is asked for. A search reads at most 20,000 tasks, or for two seconds, then answers with what it found, more, and next to go on from there. A read-only token may use it.

parameters.name: list
parameters.description: One of the app's lists: the Inbox, My Day (the Today page: picked for today, or before and not done), or Upcoming (open, with a due date).

parameters.name: view
parameters.description: A saved view's ID or name: its filter, as its page has it (top-level tasks).

parameters.name: project
parameters.description: A project's ID or name.

parameters.name: due_from
parameters.description: Due on or after this day.

parameters.name: due_to
parameters.description: Due on or before this day. Mila's This week is due_to seven days from today, overdue included.

parameters.name: words
parameters.description: Words in the title or notes, without regard to case.

parameters.name: assignee
parameters.description: Assigned to this person, by ID or name, or me. With kind=backlog,todo and me, it is the work waiting for you: an agent's queue.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: The kinds of status to keep, separated by commas: backlog, todo, in-progress, done and canceled. A task in the Inbox counts as todo while open and done once done.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: An earlier answer's next, with the same query: the tasks after where it stopped.

post.description: Puts back what a batch of yours changed through the API (writes and actions sent with Mila-Batch, or an action's own batch), newest first. Rows it made go to the trash; each field it changed goes back to what it was, unless that field has been changed since, by anyone, which is left and listed in kept. Each putting back is your own write, through the usual checks; one refused is listed in kept too. A batch can be undone for 30 days, by whoever made it. Undoing it again changes nothing more.

batch.description: The batch's name, as sent in Mila-Batch or given in an action's answer.

200.description: What was put back, and what was left.

get.description: What happened to a task, newest first.

post.description: Uploads a file (25 MB at most) and adds it to the task. The new row also arrives by sync.

get.description: A wiki page's history, newest first: its body after each editing session (one person's edits with no gap of more than five minutes), and as each body written whole (a restore, a REST write) left it. A version with no actorId is the body the page had before its history began. At most 500.

post.description: Uploads a file (25 MB at most) and adds it to the wiki page. The new row also arrives by sync.

get.description: The file of a task's attachment or a page's. Images display in the browser; everything else downloads.
The caller's API tokens that are not revoked, newest first. Not open to a token.

post.description: Makes an API token. It needs a recent sign-in, goes in the security log and emails the person. The answer holds the token, shown only this once. Not open to a token.

workspaceId.description: The one workspace it reaches. Left out

get.description: What an app connecting by OAuth asked for, for the page where the person says yes or no: its name, where it will send them, and the workspace its address named, if any. A client_id or redirect_uri that doesn't check out is refused here, and the person is never sent to it. Only when the server lets apps connect (MILA_OAUTH); not open to a token.

parameters.name: resource
parameters.description: The address the app connects to (RFC 8707), Mila's MCP endpoint.

post.description: The person's answer. Yes needs a recent sign-in and makes a code good once for ten minutes, which the app trades for a token reaching only the MCP endpoint, in the one workspace chosen; no tells the app so. Either way the answer is the address to send the person back to. Not open to a token.

workspaceId.description: The one workspace the app may reach; needed for yes.

delete.description: Stops a token working, at once. Not open to a token.

get.description: The caller's addresses that turn email into tasks in this workspace, and the mail that reached them lately. For members and above. Not open to a token.

post.description: Makes an address. It needs a recent sign-in, goes in the security log and emails the person. Not open to a token.

projectId.description: The project its tasks go to; left out or null for the Inbox.

patch.description: Changes where an address goes, and who it accepts mail from. Not open to a token.

senders.description: Addresses accepted beside the person's own.

delete.description: Ends an address, at once. Not open to a token.

post.description: Gives an address a new token, ending the old one at once and keeping its other settings. It needs a recent sign-in. Not open to a token.

get.description: The workspace's webhooks, for its owners and admins. Not open to a token.

post.description: Adds a webhook, at most 10 a workspace. The answer holds its signing secret, shown only this once. Not open to a token.

projectId.description: The one project it hears from. Left out, every project.

patch.description:
Changes what the body names. Turning one back on starts its count of
failures afresh. A new address, or turning one back on, makes the

The view's filter, under "filter": {"filter": {...}}. {} (or a null filter) shows every open task. Every part of the filter is optional, and a task must pass each part given:

- text: a string; words in the title or notes, any case.
- projects, statuses, priorities, labels, assignees: lists of strings; any one matches. projects holds project IDs or "inbox"; statuses holds status categories (backlog, todo, in-progress, done, canceled); priorities holds none, low, medium, high or urgent; labels holds label IDs; assignees holds member IDs or "me".
- statusIds: a list of status IDs; it and statuses are one part, so a task matches if its status's category is in statuses or its status is in statusIds. A finished status here shows the finished tasks in it.
- due: overdue, today (due today or before), week (within seven days), dated (has a due date) or none.
- myDay: true keeps the tasks in My Day of whoever looks, picked for today or an earlier day.
- showDone: true shows done and canceled tasks, which are otherwise hidden unless statuses or statusIds asks for them.
- dependencies: a list holding blocked (the task waits for one not done), blocking (an open task holds up one not done), or both; either matches.
- time: a list of conditions on estimates and time logged, every one of which must hold: estimated (the task has an estimate of its own), unestimated (it has none), over (more time logged on it than its estimate), recent (time logged on it in the seven days to today) and mine (time logged on it by whoever looks).
- fields: a list of conditions on custom fields, each {"field": <field ID>, "op": <operator>, "value": <what to compare with>}; every one must hold. The operators by type: text and url contains or not_contains (value: words); number eq, lt, lte, gt or gte (value: a number); date on, before, after (value: a date string, or a whole number of days from today) or between (value: two of those); select and user any or none_of (value: a list of choice or member IDs, "me" for whoever looks); multi_select any, all or none_of; checkbox checked or unchecked; and every type but checkbox empty or not_empty (no value).

A part of the wrong type is refused. At most 20,000 bytes as compact JSON.

display.description:
How the view lays out what its filter shows, or null for the defaults:

- sort: up to three rules in turn, each {"by": title, priority, due, start, created, updated, completed, status, project, estimate, logged, remaining or field, "field": <field ID> when by is field, "dir": asc or desc}. None (or by manual) is the manual order. A field to sort by is of type text, url, number, date, select, user or checkbox.
- group (list, table and timeline views): {"by": none, project, status, priority, assignee, label, due or field, "field": <ID of a select or user field>}.
- columns (board views): {"by": status, priority, due or field, "field": <ID of a select or user field>}. Status is for a project's board only, and across projects only a workspace field. due is a column for what is past, each of the next seven days, later and no date.
- fields: {"list": {"show": [...], "hide": [...]}, "board": {...}, "table": {...}}, what rows, cards and table columns show beyond each type's defaults: custom field IDs or the built-in names status, project, priority, labels, subtasks, checklist, comments, repeat, reminders, assignees, start, due, estimate, logged and remaining (the last three are a task's own estimate, the time logged on it, and what is left of the estimate). A table shows every custom field unless it is hidden.
- table (table views): {"order": [...], "widths": [{"col": ..., "px": 60 to 640}], "summaries": [{"col": ..., "fn": ...}]}: the order of the columns after the title, their widths, and what each column's summary row works out where it differs from the default (fn: none, count, filled, sum, avg, min, max, range, earliest, latest, overdue or bar). Columns are named as in fields, and the title column is "title".
- timeline (timeline views): {"zoom": day, week, month or quarter}, how much time the timeline shows across its width; week when absent.
- report (report views): {"tab": status, workload or flow, "period": weeks6, months3, year or range, "from" and "to": the days of a range, "project": a project ID or null}, how the Reports page is set up: the tab it opens on, the weeks it counts, and, for a view of no project, the one project it reports on (null for all). The view's filter narrows the tasks it counts, as everywhere.

What the app cannot use (a deleted field, a rule from a newer app) it shows as not available and otherwise ignores. At most 10,000 bytes as compact JSON.

Task.description:
A task: in a project or, with no project_id, in the inbox; with parent_id, a subtask, which lives in its parent's project.

To move a task with subtasks to another project, move the parent first (project_id, with a status_id of the new project, or null), then each subtask the same way. Page.description:
A wiki page: in a project's wiki, or with no project_id, the workspace's (which guests do not see). A wiki's main page has no parent_id and an ID made from its project's or workspace's ID (XOR with 2f5c6c0e-8a9b-4c7e-9d3a-6b1e4f2a7c58); it cannot be deleted, and its title is not shown, since it takes its project's or workspace's name. Every other page has a parent_id in the same wiki. Deleting a page does not delete its subpages: delete them too.

body is Markdown, written as the editor writes it (checklists, tables, images, and boxes as > [!NOTE]); a write replaces it whole and is kept as a version of its own in the page's history (GET .../pages/{pageId}/versions). A link to a page is a link to its address in the app (/wiki?page=<id>, or /projects/<projectId>?tab=wiki&page=<id>) and to a task is /?task=<id>; when either is renamed, links whose text was its old name take the new one. An image of a file attached to the page or a task is ![name](/api/v1/workspaces/<workspaceId>/attachments/<attachmentId>/file).
